name: Motorcycle
description: A motor vehicle with a seat or saddle, no more than three wheels on the ground, and a motor that displaces more than 250 cc. Arkansas has no separate electric motorcycle or off-highway motorcycle category, and the statute sets no electric power or speed equivalent of its displacement line.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
Its motor displaces more than 250 cc; the statute gives no electric equivalent, so it doesn't say which electric motors fall here rather than under motor-driven cycle
Riders need a motorcycle operator's license (Class M, 16 or older), earned with a written exam, a vision test and a road test, which an MSF rider course within 90 days waives
Can't be sold to anyone under 16
Riders and passengers under 21 must wear protective headgear, and every rider and passenger must wear protective glasses, goggles or a transparent face shield
Needs a headlight, a rear red reflector and red tail lamp, brakes, a horn, a muffler, electric turn signals, and passenger handholds and footrests if built to carry one
Registered yearly with the Department of Finance and Administration, carries a license plate, and must carry liability insurance

One designed or manufactured exclusively for competition or off-road use, such as an electric dirt bike, isn't required to be registered; Arkansas has no off-highway motorcycle registration or sticker
Arkansas's all-terrain vehicle law covers only vehicles with three or more low-pressure tires, so it doesn't reach a two-wheeled off-road motorcycle
These rules don't apply when ridden on a farm or on private property
